catalog_quote: [p. xix] En palabras polisilábicas hay una restricción en la concurrencia de sílabas que llevan el tono ⁵. La raíz de una palabra es la sílaba que lleva el acento fonético (la sílaba que lleva mayor fuerza o énfasis). A la raíz son añadidos los prefijos o sufijos necesarios. Cuando un prefijo con tono ⁵ va antes de una raíz con tono ⁵, el tono del prefijo cambia a tono ⁴. Es decir, una sílaba que no lleva el acento fonético, pero que lleva el tono ⁵, tiene que cambiarse al tono ⁴ antes de una raíz con el acento fonético y con el tono ⁵. Por ejemplo, en lugar de decir *ma⁵lie⁵i³ empezará, se dice ma⁴lie⁵i³. [p. xv] Como se ve, la primera sílaba varía en pronunciación. new_statements.translation: In polysyllabic words there is a restriction on the co-occurrence of syllables bearing tone 5. The root of a word is the syllable that carries the phonetic accent (the syllable with the greatest force or emphasis). The necessary prefixes or suffixes are added to the root. When a prefix with tone 5 precedes a root with tone 5, the prefix tone changes to tone 4. That is, a syllable that does not carry the phonetic accent but carries tone 5 must change to tone 4 before a root with the phonetic accent and tone 5. [p. xv:] Fortunately, the first syllable in nouns is not as important as the final one, which is the root of the word.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Usila Chinantec is a five-level tone language; word stress ('acento fonético') falls on the root syllable, to which unstressed prefixes (classifiers, TAM prefixes) and suffixes attach; in nouns the root is the final syllable, so stress is typically word-final/root-final with pretonic prefixes. Stress is stated as a property of the root, not computed by syllable count or weight.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated for native words. Person suffixes/enclitic tones (-i³, tone-substituted pronouns) follow the root, so stress is not strictly word-final in suffixed verbs. Spanish loans keep their Spanish stress position, marked tonally (penult stress -> tone 2 on that syllable, final stress -> tone 23; Gramática sec. 24, pp. 572-573).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement made in passing within the tone description (to explain a tone-5 dissimilation on unstressed prefixes); no dedicated stress section, no mention of ballistic vs controlled syllables in this source. Popular-audience dictionary front matter, but first-hand by the SIL fieldworkers who described the language (Skinner 1962).
new_statements.identity_note: Source describes the Chinantec of San Felipe Usila municipality and nearby settlements (plus relocated speakers in Uxpanapa, Veracruz) = Glottolog usil1237 / ISO cuc exactly; authors note two sub-dialects differing in pretonic-syllable vowels (o- vs u-), irrelevant to the stress statement.
